routesElsewhere.note: Accounts receive the request; the School Admin approves it, because a plan changes when the school is paid (BR-3).
The schedule is defined after the request is approved, never before (E9).
A plan schedules a debt. It never changes how much is owed, only when it is paid (BR-1).
While a plan is being met no late fee accrues at all (BR-7) — but a fine already applied is waived separately.

steps.note: One step, producing a request at Requested. No schedule exists, the charge is unchanged and the family is still in overdue tracking until a plan is approved and active (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An active plan on the same charge, and an invoice already paid, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request with the family's stated reason, together with the audit entry or not at all. The invoice is unchanged (BR-6), no protection applies yet, and the family is still chased and still accruing late fee until a plan is approved and active (BR-7).

errors.meaning: An active plan already exists for the charge.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. It is what the School Admin weighs (BR-2), and a request with no reason cannot be judged — a planner's version describes what it inferred about a family's circumstances.

Never chain the approval or the schedule. Accounts receive, the School Admin approves, Accounts define — three acts, because a plan changes when the school is paid (BR-3), and defining before approval is refused outright (E9).
Never describe the request as protecting the family yet. Nothing applies until a plan is approved and active (BR-7); until then they are still on the overdue list and still accruing late fee.
Never treat a plan as a reduction. It schedules a debt and never changes how much is owed (BR-1) — a family asking to pay less is asking for a concession.

routesElsewhere.note: The installments must total exactly the outstanding charge (BR-4). Reducing one means raising another, which is a reschedule.

steps.note: One step, and it activates the plan. From here the student leaves overdue tracking, is not reminded and accrues no late fee while the plan is met — which is the whole point of agreeing one (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Installments that do not total the charge, dates out of order, dates outside the session, fewer than two installments and an unapproved request are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the plan, all its installments and the audit entry together or not at all. The original invoice is unchanged — the plan sits against it and the challan reflects the plan, but the charge itself is untouched (BR-6). Activating it removes the student from overdue tracking, stops reminders and stops late fee accruing, for as long as the plan is met (BR-7); a single missed installment ends all of that at once (BR-8).

operations.name: fee.plan.define
operations.idempotencyKey: plan_request_id, since an approved request produces one plan
operations.purpose: Define the installments of an approved request and activate the plan.

parameters.name: plan_request_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No plan request matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and status.

parameters.notes: The plan request, resolved from how the actor named it — the student, the invoice, or the reference.

parameters.name: installments
parameters.notes: Two or more, each with an amount and a due date. They must total exactly the outstanding charge — a plan that adds up to less is a discount granted by arithmetic (BR-4, E1). Each falls due later than the one before, and all within the academic session (BR-5, E2, E3). Every figure and every date comes from the request.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: invoice_status
fields.description: Unchanged. The plan sits against the invoice (BR-6).

fields.name: removed_from_overdue
fields.description: True. The student leaves overdue tracking and accrues no late fee while the plan is met (BR-7).

fields.name: next_installment
fields.description: Amount and date, so whoever answers the counter can see it (BR-12).

errors.meaning: The installments do not total the outstanding charge.
errors.note: The message names both figures. A plan that adds up to less is a discount granted by arithmetic (BR-4) — never adjust an installment to make it balance.

errors.meaning: An installment falls due before the one before it.
An installment falls outside the academic session.
errors.note: A debt carried past the session it arose in is a different problem (BR-5).

errors.meaning: Fewer than two installments were defined.
errors.note: One payment is not a plan.

errors.meaning: The request has not been approved.
errors.note: Approval comes first, by the School Admin (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never supply, adjust or round an installment amount. They must total exactly the outstanding charge (BR-4), and a figure a planner nudges to make the arithmetic work is a discount or a surcharge nobody agreed.
Never supply the due dates. They are what the family committed to, and a schedule invented here commits them to dates nobody discussed.
Never define a plan before the request is approved. E9 is BR-3 working — a plan changes when the school is paid, so somebody else agrees to it first.

Report that the protection now applies, and that one missed installment ends it. While the plan is met the student is out of overdue tracking with no late fee (BR-7); a plan being broken is not a plan being kept, and the protection ends at once (BR-8).
Report the next installment. Whoever answers the counter needs it, so a family paying as agreed is never told they are in arrears by somebody who did not know (BR-12).
Never describe the plan as changing what is owed. It schedules a debt and nothing more (BR-1), and the invoice is untouched (BR-6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An active plan is not deleted. It is rescheduled through fee.plan.reschedule, with a written reason and a schedule that still totals the original charge (BR-10). Where the family stops paying altogether the plan is missed and the protection ends (BR-8) — the debt was never reduced. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.
